angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 150,410 km at 14.64 pc = 0.14 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 68.2986 +/- 0.0652 mas (same row, RUWE 1.01): 14.64 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.2162 +/- 0.0025 solar radii from Mahajan et al. 2024, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of GJ 1214 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024ApJ...963L..37M/abstract): 150,410 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.182 +/- 0.0042 solar masses from Mahajan et al. 2024, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of GJ 1214 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024ApJ...963L..37M/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3101 +/- 43 K from Mahajan et al. 2024, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of GJ 1214 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024ApJ...963L..37M/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Mahajan et al. 2024, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of GJ 1214 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024ApJ...963L..37M/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/gj-1214.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 5.028, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
